reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial explicitly measured NF-κB inhibition as a biomarker of proteasome engagement. Results showed 0/19 patients in Phase I and 0/28 patients in Phase II achieved ≥50% NF-κB inhibition, indicating no meaningful target engagement despite reaching the MTD of bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: With no target engagement confirmed, downstream pathway modulation was not achieved. NF-κB activation measured in peripheral blood mononuclear cells showed no significant inhibition. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Clinical outcomes were poor - Phase I had 4/19 partial responses (21% ORR), Phase II had only 1/28 partial responses (3.6% ORR). The majority of patients had progressive disease (14/19 in Phase I, 22/28 in Phase II). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup differences were observed - both phases showed predominantly progressive disease. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was adequately designed as a dose-escalation study that established MTD, but the fundamental issue was lack of target engagement at tolerable doses.
